title_cyr: Ајде што ти текна што побегна
title_latin: Ajde što ti tekna što pobegna
title_en: Come On, What Came Over You That You Ran Away
background: A cheeky wedding song. A young bride runs away from her marital home before dawn, and everyone guesses why: the house is fine, the father-in-law is a tame lamb, the mother-in-law is a hot snake. The real reason, the last verse says, is the young husband himself. It is played at weddings amid howls of laughter. A second version of the song is under #772.
background_source: Source of these notes: Qwen's draft.
en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: 'Непропеани' I read as 'not yet crowed' (of roosters). No other guessed lines.

words_to_learn.en: occurred to you, came over you

lines.cyr: Ајде што ти текна што побегна
lines.lat: Ajde što ti tekna što pobegna
lines.en: Come on, what came over you that you ran away
in the early morning at dawn?
Come on, in the early morning at dawn,
when the roosters had not yet crowed.
Come on, did you not like the house,
or the father-in-law, or the mother-in-law?
Come on, did you not like the house,
or the father-in-law, or the mother-in-law?
Come on, the house is very good,
the father-in-law is a gentle lamb.
Come on, the father-in-law is a gentle lamb,
but the mother-in-law is a fierce snake.
